title: Representations converge across models
description: Different models learn increasingly similar representations as capability grows.

coverage.scope_note: This snapshot contains the saved merged final records used by this entry, including records not individually shown on the page. It is not an exhaustive collection of experiments or papers. Missing records, omitted extraction and not-tested statements are different from negative results.

claims.heading: Representations become more aligned as models grow larger and more capable
Better vision and language models align more on paired images and captions
Networks trained from different seeds can share features and subspaces
Simple mappings can make representations interchangeable across models
Some interpretable features and circuits recur across models
Measured convergence depends on the similarity metric, its settings and the test inputs
Incomplete representation alignment results from shared training rather than shared structure in the world

related_findings.title: Similarity depends on how representations are measured
related_findings.summary: Similarity scores vary with the transformations a metric ignores, the number of dimensions, the samples used and preprocessing. Scores can miss structural changes or change in response to irrelevant variance.

examples.headline: Generated-token pooling yields higher LLM-to-DINOv2 debiased CKA than prompt tokens on WIT.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Correspondence depends on model design and training
related_findings.summary: Models can share representational structure even when no scaling trend has been demonstrated. How strongly they correspond, and at which depths, varies with architecture, which earlier models they derive from, training and how representations are extracted.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Similar geometry does not establish shared function
related_findings.summary: Geometric similarity, decodable information, causal interchangeability and parameter correspondence can dissociate. Transfer also depends on how representations are decoded or intervened on.

examples.headline: Near-perfect teacher CKA coexists with severe functional failure after reinitialization.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Mapping direction and fitting conditions affect success
related_findings.summary: Mappings between models can enable transfer, retrieval and linking representations to their referents. Success varies with the information available, which model is mapped to which, coverage by reference examples, representation geometry, preprocessing and optimization.

examples.headline: Qwen2.5-1.5B's representation coordinates match a fixed reference more closely when more tokens are used.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Similarity predicts behavior under specific conditions
related_findings.summary: How similar representations are can predict agreement in model behavior, compatibility for transfer and performance. These links can be weak or absent, and vary with the similarity metric, task, domain, architecture and models compared.

examples.headline: Of the tested similarity metrics, Procrustes correlates most strongly with similarity in model behavior.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training preserves some structure while reorganizing other parts
related_findings.summary: Some geometry and features persist through training or adaptation even as selected layers and subspaces reorganize. The changes vary with training stage, task, modality and adaptation method.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Language alignment varies across layers and languages
related_findings.summary: A multilingual model can represent equivalent content similarly across languages. The match varies across layers, with language resources, writing system, training and content, and does not increase uniformly with model size.

examples.headline: In Qwen2.5-0.5B, similarity between translated sentences' representations peaks at the middle layers among those reported.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Modalities share structure at different depths
related_findings.summary: Within a shared model, different modalities or views can develop partly matching representations of meaning and tasks. Where these matches occur across layers, and how accessible they are for functional use, varies with architecture, training objective and the procedure used to align representations.

examples.headline: Substituting text-derived digit representations into Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B's image-token states changes arithmetic answers in over 90% of cases.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Task success does not identify internal geometry
related_findings.summary: Models with different internal geometry can match in accuracy or outputs, or work when their parts are joined. Such success does not establish shared geometry: the evidence depends on the decoding method's flexibility, the coverage of representations tested and the tasks' ability to distinguish cases.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Biological alignment varies across comparisons
related_findings.summary: How closely models match biological representations varies across regions, layers, stimuli and measurement choices. Some comparisons give stable results across the tested measures.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Multimodal alignment depends on training and domain
related_findings.summary: Training objectives that link modalities and learned connector modules can create useful but selective matches between representations. Larger backbones or higher similarity do not necessarily improve retrieval or task performance.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Predictive agreement depends on task and training
related_findings.summary: Models can rank outputs similarly, make similar errors, learn in a similar order or produce similar predictive distributions even without an established mapping between their representations. Agreement varies with inputs, architecture, training, confidence and scale.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training shapes correspondence with biology and human judgments
related_findings.summary: Training objectives, initialization, data and how representations are processed affect how closely models match biological or human representations. Targeted fine-tuning does not necessarily improve the match.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Teacher supervision aligns selected representations
related_findings.summary: Supervision using features and shared latent targets can produce representations like a teacher's and enable useful transfer. Effects vary across modules, channels and input regions, and with architecture, loss and how gradients propagate.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Parameter alignment can improve weight merging and connectivity
related_findings.summary: Aligning parameters by permutation, sign changes or linear transformations, and repairing normalization, can improve weight merging and connections between models through low-loss paths in parameter space. Results vary with architecture, width, depth, task and training.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Capability gains do not always improve biological alignment
related_findings.summary: Correspondence with biological responses or human judgments can plateau or decline as capability or parameter size increases. The relationship varies by model family, task and alignment target.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Semantic sharing depends on context and format
related_findings.summary: Within a model, the same structure for representing meaning can serve different contexts, formats and related tasks. Surface form, tokenization, input order and conflicts between tasks can limit feature sharing and whether causal interventions transfer.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Recurring circuit roles have different implementations
related_findings.summary: Concept detectors and circuits serving the same roles can recur across models. Architecture, scale and task competence affect their abundance, the depths at which they occur, their specialization and whether individual units match.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Artificial representations only partly match biological representations
related_findings.summary: Artificial representations can partly match biological representations, perceptual structure or human semantic structure. Correspondence can also be weak, absent, fail to preserve distances or omit selected parts.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Independent modalities can share partial structure
related_findings.summary: Models trained independently on different modalities can share relations among representations, semantic axes or spatial organization even when no scaling trend has been demonstrated. The match varies with layer, training objective and which model is mapped to which.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Similar overall profiles do not establish matching features
related_findings.summary: Models with different random seeds or architectures can show similar profiles of complexity, interpretability, brain alignment or processing stages. These similarities can coexist with differences in retained information and do not establish that individual features match.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Abstraction within models can strengthen or plateau
related_findings.summary: Semantic organization, abstraction of relations and structure that probes can detect can strengthen or plateau with size, capability or training. Results vary with training objective, layer, how representations are extracted and the stimuli used.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Causal interventions can transfer after alignment
related_findings.summary: Features shared across models, or mapped between them, can let causal interventions transfer between models. Whether steering transfers varies with how coordinate systems are aligned, shared input and output directions, which way transfer runs, the target model's capability and the task.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Stronger alignment can erase information specific to one modality
related_findings.summary: Multimodal representations contain both shared structure and information specific to one modality. Enforcing stronger alignment can discard modality-specific information, which can help or hurt according to its relevance to the task.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Raw embedding coordinates are generally not interchangeable
related_findings.summary: Independently trained models generally need a mapping or a mechanism designed for compatibility to use one another's raw embeddings. Some models also lose direct compatibility between embedding coordinates after sequential updates.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Shared components can promote coordinate compatibility
related_findings.summary: Models that share initialization, layers, heads or input components can develop compatible coordinates. Nonlinearities and input geometry limit which changes of coordinate system a model can accommodate.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Networks contain overlapping internal representations
related_findings.summary: Within a network, features, experts, heads, layers and subspaces can overlap in what they represent, sometimes allowing compression. How much is redundant varies with architecture, depth, shared inputs and training.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Scale and training can improve biological alignment
related_findings.summary: In certain language, vision and audio settings, models match biological responses more closely as model size, capability or training progress increases. Gains sometimes diminish.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training objectives shape shared invariances
related_findings.summary: Training objectives and imposed symmetries shape which changes models ignore in common. In the tested settings, adversarial training, training models to teach one another, and language guidance can increase this invariance or the correspondence between models' functions.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Some representational similarity appears before learning
related_findings.summary: Even without training, architecture, initialization and shared low-level input geometry can make models' representations appear to correspond. Comparisons between trained and random models also reveal shared structures absent from the random models.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Shared concepts do not establish identical features
related_findings.summary: Models can share directions representing concepts, relations among representations or attributes recoverable by decoding, sometimes after mapping representations or fitting separate axes. This does not establish identical features, coordinates or functional use.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Shared dimensions can carry important information
related_findings.summary: Dimensions shared across models can capture high-level meaning and correspond more strongly to biological vision or human judgments. They can also matter more for computation or causal effects.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Cross-language training signals can increase alignment
related_findings.summary: Sharing parameters, using words as reference points and imposing explicit training constraints can increase alignment between languages within a model. Effects vary with layer, language and domain.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Similar geometry across languages need not mean shared coordinates
related_findings.summary: How similar languages' representations appear varies with how token representations are pooled, tokenization, the number of independent dimensions (rank), layer and the transformations the comparison permits. Similar geometry does not ensure shared coordinates without training signals that link languages.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Sparse autoencoder dictionaries are only partly reproducible
related_findings.summary: Sparse autoencoders trained on the same fixed activations recover feature dictionaries that overlap but differ. How reproducible the dictionaries are varies with sparsity, dictionary size, model size, feature quality, training data and filtering.

examples.headline: Across seeds, Qwen3-1.7B sparse-autoencoder features correlate at 0.871 when each is the other's closest match.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Shared structure can accompany adversarial transfer
related_findings.summary: Shared features, overlapping training data or distillation can occur alongside adversarial effects that transfer between models. Transfer varies with layer, the source model's robustness, the model pair and training that encourages diversity.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Some stimuli elicit more consistent representations
related_findings.summary: Models represent some stimuli more consistently than others, with variation related to how typical or predictable the stimuli are. Some of this variation generalizes across model groups, can be predicted from a single model and changes with targeted fine-tuning.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Communication can synchronize agents
related_findings.summary: Training agents to communicate, or letting them interact, can align their representations, messages, predictions or beliefs. In the tested settings, alignment relates to cooperation and social performance and can coincide with reduced novelty at the group level.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Shared dynamics depend on task and training
related_findings.summary: Recurrent systems and systems with latent states can develop shared dynamical solutions when trained on tasks. In coupled Q-networks, similarity can fluctuate during training and coincide with lower returns from the ensemble.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Representations become stable at different times
related_findings.summary: Representations can settle into a stable form before training ends, often earlier in shallower layers. Warmup and learning-rate schedules affect how this stabilization unfolds.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Attention profiles share coarse patterns
related_findings.summary: Models can share broad patterns of attention or how tokens influence processing, with similar developmental timing, while differing in head placement and fine detail. Agreement varies with training, size, inputs and how the profiles are constructed.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Intrinsic dimension captures some shared complexity
related_findings.summary: Models can share patterns in the number of dimensions needed to describe their representations. Links between lower intrinsic dimension, semantic coherence and alignment vary with the model and the scale of the local neighborhood measured.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Human representational geometry can match across modalities and people
related_findings.summary: Human representations can have similar geometry across modalities and people even when their spatial layouts in the cortex differ. The match varies with region, architectural constraints and the alignment procedure.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Data and regularization shape alignment
related_findings.summary: How similar models' representations are depends on how inputs are represented, shared vocabulary or structure, data quality and amount, and regularization. Capability alone does not determine this similarity.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Shared structure covers some attributes and misses others
related_findings.summary: Features that recur across models can support specialized applications, but the parts of their representations that they share leave out other attributes. Models from the same family can also fail to capture the same physical properties.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Languages share some features and control mechanisms
related_findings.summary: Languages within a multilingual model share some register, discourse, reasoning and output-language features or controls. Sharing varies by model, layer and modality.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Joint training can align dictionary codes
related_findings.summary: Training dictionaries (learned feature sets) jointly or in pairs can make their features line up, even when reconstructing data or matching distributions alone does not reveal how they correspond. Concepts learned jointly only partly match those in independently learned dictionaries.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Weight convergence can differ from functional convergence
related_findings.summary: Accounting for permutation symmetry reveals task-related weight regularities across seeds. Weight convergence can lag functional learning or change differently from dynamical convergence.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Shared internal structure requires additional assumptions
related_findings.summary: Theoretical guarantees of shared kernels or translatable internal states require specific optimization, redundancy, minimality or interface conditions. Equivalent observable dynamics alone do not identify shared internal structure.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Architecture shapes how representations encode symmetries
related_findings.summary: Representations can encode input symmetries through equivariant transformations. Whether symmetry is preserved or violated depends on architecture, layer and training.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Simplified theories identify possible sources of convergence
related_findings.summary: Simplified theoretical models connect shared representations or patterns in how learning unfolds to what models can express, small initial weights and the way SGD favors some solutions over others. These theories rely on assumptions that differ from those behind general empirical claims of convergence.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Models retain useful complementary information
related_findings.summary: Combining models, or joining parts of different models (stitching), can use predictions and information that one model provides and another lacks. The similarity between two models' representations does not necessarily predict how much they complement each other.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Shared noise can yield similar diffusion outputs
related_findings.summary: Diffusion models can produce similar outputs from shared noise in particular regimes. Architecture, task difficulty, fine-tuning and training data can produce systematic differences.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Text representations can encode temporal regularities
related_findings.summary: Text representations can reflect patterns over time associated with numerical sequences. Components pretrained on language can encode such patterns in a form that can be read out, along with information about how a sequence continues.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

reading_list.why: Introduces alignment linked to model performance, within vision and across modalities, with early evidence that similarity metric choices matter.
Separates matching individual CNN units from learning mappings that connect one network's representations to another's.
Baseline correction removes some centered kernel alignment (CKA) scaling trends but preserves a trend in models' shared nearest neighbors.

known_gaps.summary: Open questions concern scaling and saturation, cross-modal scope, stitching and transfer conditions, independent replication, coverage of the largest models, verification of extracted results and incomplete claim summaries.
items: Whether alignment grows or levels off as models scale remains unresolved across model families, metrics and comparison settings. Correcting for baseline effects removes some centered kernel alignment (CKA) trends, but a trend in Pythia models survives, and measures that compare nearby representations can retain scaling trends.

How far convergence extends across modalities remains unclear: in 3D–text results, more complex encoders do not improve alignment, and some comparisons show large errors in how well geometry matches across modalities.

ResNet-18 studies reach opposing results when joining parts of different models (stitching), but test different connection points, including between blocks and inside residual blocks. It has not been established whether these studies used identical connection points and optimization procedures.

Conclusions about transfer still need to account for which model transfers to which and how capable the receiving model already is. Comparisons across Llama model sizes need a baseline: the performance of a probe trained directly on each receiving model.

Independent replication is still uncertain for several claims. Some supporting studies share authors with the original work, and author independence has not been checked across several broader groups of findings.
Evidence coverage above 100B parameters remains uncertain because sizes are unspecified for some frontier and API models. Missing size information does not establish that this scale is untested.

Some figure-dependent results remain unverified because extraction obscured which coefficients belonged to which comparisons. Corrected evidence summaries also lack a second verification pass. Some reviewed findings on stitching, input dependence and small-sample comparisons are also missing from the claim summaries.
